title: You Don’t Need All That Attention: Surgical Memorization Mitigation in Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
claim: Memorized prompts show distinctive attention patterns, concentrated on a few tokens and persistently high at the end token, which separate them from non-memorized prompts.
layout: 2x2 grid of line plots; top: per-token distribution, bottom: per-step trend
description: A 2x2 grid of line plots with shaded areas under the curves and dashed grid lines. The top row, panels (a) VM and (b) TM, plots cross-attention mass against token position (1 to 75). Blue marks the first inference step and red marks the last. A dashed vertical line labeled 'EOT token' marks the end of the prompt. Panel (a) has a sharp peak near token 13, and panel (b) has a peak near token 1. Both curves flatten to a low tail. The bottom row, panels (c) VM and (d) TM, plots cross-attention mass at EOT against inference step (0 to 49). A blue line is the memorized prompt and an orange line is the non-memorized prompt, with a shaded gap between them. In (c) the memorized curve stays well above the non-memorized one. In (d) the memorized curve starts lower, then the two converge. Captions sit under each panel.
caption: CA patterns. (a) and (b): the CA mass across tokens, in the first and last inference steps for verbatim and template memorization (VM and TM). For clarity, we exclude the first token (position 0) from the plots, as it consistently receives the majority of CA across both memorized and non-memorized examples, which would dominate the scale and obscure differences among the remaining tokens. (c) and (d): the CA mass on EOT across steps, for a memorized and a non-memorized prompt. (c): VM on SD v1.4. (d): TM on SD v2.0.
abstract: Generative models have been shown to "memorize" certain training data, leading to verbatim or near-verbatim generating images, which may cause privacy concerns or copyright infringement. We introduce Guidance Using Attractive-Repulsive Dynamics (GUARD), a novel framework for memorization mitigation in text-to-image diffusion models. GUARD adjusts the image denoising process to guide the generation away from an original training image and towards one that is distinct from training data while remaining aligned with the prompt, guarding against reproducing training data, without hurting image generation quality. We propose a concrete instantiation of this framework, where the positive target that we steer towards is given by a novel method for (cross) attention attenuation based on (i) a novel statistical mechanism that automatically identifies the prompt positions where cross attention must be attenuated and (ii) attenuating cross-attention in these per-prompt locations. The resulting GUARD offers a surgical, dynamic per-prompt inference-time approach that, we find, is by far the most robust method in terms of consistently producing state-of-the-art results for memorization mitigation across two architectures and for both verbatim and template memorization, while also improving upon or yielding comparable results in terms of image quality.
